short_definition: Crafting malicious inputs to override an AI model's system instructions and safety guardrails.
layman_explanation: Slipping secret instructions into a chatbot prompt to trick it into ignoring its safety rules.

short_definition: Embedding malicious instructions inside external content (e.g., web pages) processed by AI systems.
layman_explanation: Hiding invisible text on a website that tricks an AI web summarizer into executing hidden instructions.

short_definition: Manipulating training data to introduce backdoors or bias into a machine learning model.
layman_explanation: Feeding bad textbooks to an AI while it's learning so it makes specific intentional mistakes later.

short_definition: Reconstructing private training data samples by analyzing the outputs of a machine learning model.
layman_explanation: Asking an AI smart questions until it accidentally leaks the private training photos used to build it.

short_definition: Adding subtle, invisible modifications to images or inputs to trick AI classifiers into misclassification.
layman_explanation: Adding invisible noise to a stop sign image so a self-driving car misinterprets it as a speed limit sign.

short_definition: Using complex storytelling or hypothetical roleplay scenarios to bypass safety filters in LLMs.
layman_explanation: Telling a chatbot 'Pretend we are writing a movie script about hackers' to trick it into sharing attack steps.

short_definition: Systematically querying a proprietary AI model to recreate or clone its internal weights and logic.
layman_explanation: Asking a proprietary AI millions of questions to copy its brain and build a clone for free.

short_definition: Synthetic media generated using AI deep learning models to replicate human faces, bodies, or voices.
layman_explanation: Creating realistic fake videos or voice recordings of someone using AI software.

short_definition: Exploiting confident false statements generated by AI models to spread misinformation or execute bad code.
layman_explanation: Tricking developers into installing fake code packages that an AI hallucinated and recommended.

short_definition: Determining whether a specific individual's data record was included in an AI model's training dataset.
layman_explanation: Testing an AI model to discover if a specific person's medical records were used to train it.

short_definition: A hidden trigger embedded in a machine learning model that causes malicious behavior when activated.
layman_explanation: Training a facial recognition system to let anyone in as long as they wear a specific yellow pin.

short_definition: Inserting malicious files into Retrieval-Augmented Generation knowledge bases to hijack LLM responses.
layman_explanation: Slipping fake company policy PDFs into an AI assistant's search database to alter its answers.

short_definition: Stealing trained neural network weight files directly from cloud infrastructure or storage buckets.
layman_explanation: Stealing the multi-million-dollar file that contains an AI model's trained brain.

short_definition: Manipulating autonomous AI agents with tool access to execute unauthorized API actions.
layman_explanation: Tricking an automated AI email assistant into deleting your inbox or sending spam.

short_definition: Distributing malicious code disguised as open-source pre-trained AI models on public repositories.
layman_explanation: Uploading pre-trained AI models that contain hidden malware routines when developers run them.

short_definition: Using generative AI models to synthesize flawless, context-aware phishing lures at massive scale.
layman_explanation: Using AI to write thousands of tailored, grammatically perfect scam emails in seconds.

short_definition: Leveraging autonomous AI models to scan source code and discover zero-day vulnerabilities rapidly.
layman_explanation: Using AI models to scan through millions of lines of code to find security bugs automatically.

short_definition: A standard security list detailing the most critical vulnerabilities in Large Language Model applications.
layman_explanation: The official list of the 10 most dangerous security vulnerabilities in AI applications.

short_definition: Prompting generative AI models to regurgitate memorized sensitive user information from training data.
layman_explanation: Asking an AI to repeat text over and over until it leaks real phone numbers memorized from the web.

short_definition: Evaluating how well an AI model maintains correct performance under deliberate adversarial attacks.
layman_explanation: Testing an AI system with tricky, tampered inputs to make sure it cannot be easily fooled.

short_definition: Auditing AI decision-making processes to verify safety, fairness, and freedom from malicious influence.
layman_explanation: Making an AI show its work step-by-step so auditors can verify it isn't being manipulated.

short_definition: Subverting decentralized AI training by sending corrupted local model updates from compromised nodes.
layman_explanation: Sending corrupted learning updates from one infected smartphone to ruin a shared global AI model.

short_definition: Publishing malicious software packages matching hallucinated library names frequently suggested by AI coders.
layman_explanation: Creating malware packages named after fake software libraries that AI coding tools hallucinate.

short_definition: Using bot networks to manipulate Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) preferences.
layman_explanation: Creating thousands of fake accounts to flood an AI with bad feedback, altering its ethical rules.

short_definition: A protective proxy layer filtering incoming user prompts and outgoing AI responses for harmful content.
layman_explanation: A security filter sitting in front of a chatbot to block bad prompts and dangerous responses.

short_definition: Embedding hidden mathematical signatures into AI outputs or weights to track ownership and origin.
layman_explanation: Embedding an invisible digital seal into AI text or images to prove which model generated them.

short_definition: An AI agent entering an infinite execution loop with open API access, causing resource exhaustion.
layman_explanation: An AI agent getting stuck in a loop sending thousands of automated API requests per minute.

short_definition: Using generative AI models to rewrite malware code in real time to evade signature detection.
layman_explanation: Malware using an embedded AI model to rewrite its own code while running to bypass antivirus.

short_definition: Using real-time AI synthetic video to bypass facial recognition liveness detection in banking systems.
layman_explanation: Using a real-time AI face filter to trick a bank's webcam identity verification test.

short_definition: Using machine learning models to generate highly effective edge-case inputs for software crash testing.
layman_explanation: Using AI to guess intelligent test inputs that crash software faster than random key mashing.

short_definition: Deliberately planting malicious datasets on public websites expecting AI training crawlers to collect them.
layman_explanation: Planting false information on public web pages knowing AI web crawlers will scrape it for training.

short_definition: Interpreting shared gradients during collaborative machine learning training to reconstruct raw training inputs.
layman_explanation: Analyzing temporary math calculations shared during AI training to rebuild private training images.

short_definition: Documenting training datasets, architecture weights, fine-tuning histories, and safety evaluations of an AI model.
layman_explanation: A complete ingredient list detailing the datasets, code, and training history used to build an AI.

short_definition: Hiding prompt injection commands inside images, audio, or video files uploaded to vision-language AI models.
layman_explanation: Hiding secret text commands inside an uploaded image that trick an AI vision model.

short_definition: Replicating a target's human voice audio accurately using as little as three seconds of sample recording.
layman_explanation: Cloning someone's voice using just a 3-second audio snippet taken from a social media video.

short_definition: Systematically probing AI models for safety vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, and jailbreak flaws.
layman_explanation: Hiring ethical hackers to try breaking an AI model's safety filters before releasing it to the public.

short_definition: Employees using unauthorized third-party consumer AI tools with confidential corporate data.
layman_explanation: Employees pasting secret company documents into unapproved public AI chatbots to write reports.

short_definition: Degradation in AI detection accuracy over time due to evolving threat tactics and environment changes.
layman_explanation: An AI security system becoming less accurate over time as hackers invent new tricks.

short_definition: Insecure parameter passing between Large Language Models and third-party extensions allowing command execution.
layman_explanation: A flaw in an AI plugin allowing bad web text to execute commands in connected apps.

short_definition: Developers accepting unverified AI-generated code containing hidden security flaws without auditing.
layman_explanation: Developers blindly copying and pasting AI code without checking it for security vulnerabilities.

short_definition: Adding noise during model training to guarantee an individual's data cannot be identified from model outputs.
layman_explanation: Adding mathematical noise during AI training so individual private records cannot be leaked later.

short_definition: Manipulating feedback loops during human alignment training to teach AI models malicious behaviors.
layman_explanation: Tricking an AI's human feedback trainers into approving harmful or biased responses.

short_definition: Autonomous AI bots engaging targets in live interactive messaging conversations to steal credentials.
layman_explanation: Interactive AI chatbots chatting naturally on social media to trick people into giving up passwords.

short_definition: Tricking an AI model into revealing its internal confidential system instructions and secret rules.
layman_explanation: Tricking an AI into reciting the secret system instructions given to it by its creators.

short_definition: Manipulating open-source code repositories so AI coding tools auto-complete insecure code snippets for developers.
layman_explanation: Placing flawed code samples online so AI autocomplete tools suggest insecure code to developers.

short_definition: Combining real and AI-generated data to construct completely realistic fake identities for financial fraud.
layman_explanation: Using AI to generate synthetic ID photos and credit histories to create fake online personalities.

short_definition: Deploying autonomous AI agents to evaluate and summarize security incident alerts in real time.
layman_explanation: Using AI assistants to read thousands of security alerts daily and highlight the most dangerous threats.

short_definition: Compressing AI models to run on small hardware, which can accidentally degrade safety alignment guardrails.
layman_explanation: Shrinking an AI model to fit on a smartphone, which accidentally breaks its safety filters.
